title: Molecular representations and physical prediction
summary: I investigate when learned molecular representations help physical prediction. My work combines encoder comparisons, controlled ablations, and physical readouts, progressing from CG polymer and MACE water studies to controlled-response experiments and current pretrained-feature transfer research.
question: Which physical information survives representation learning, and when does it improve prediction beyond matched baselines?
progression: CG and MACE JEPA → controlled-response tests and pretrained-feature transfer
cvSummary: Encoder comparisons, representation ablations, and physical-readout evaluation, from earlier CG polymer and MACE water studies to current pretrained-feature transfer research.

stages.label: Current direction
stages.context: This current branch compares pretrained and randomly initialized encoders for QM9 property prediction, with matched data and downstream update budgets. It also includes preparation for crystal-property transfer and label-efficiency studies.

stages.label: Recent completed study
stages.context: This completed study tested state/control adaptations and functional readouts on a synthetic hysteretic system. It extends the earlier representation questions into predictions under alternative control programs.

stages.label: Earlier exploration · closed
stages.context: This atomistic-water phase followed the CG encoder comparison and closed on 9 October 2026. The adapters, temporal controls, and physical-readout analyses informed later response and transfer questions.

stages.label: Earlier exploration · completed
stages.context: The original CG polymer study examined geometric interfaces, physical readouts, and temporal learning. It motivated the subsequent MACE encoder comparison and broader questions about physically useful representations.

title: MLIP material properties and efficiency
summary: I build and evaluate polymer-property workflows and measure their computational cost. Current work connects classical preparation, MACE density simulations, sampling checks, and reference comparisons; GPU allocation studies examine the resource-efficiency questions raised by earlier UMA / FAIR-Chem work.
question: How can ML interatomic potentials support credible material-property calculations within practical compute and memory budgets?
progression: UMA / FAIR-Chem exploration → MACE property simulations → GPU resource evaluation
cvSummary: Polymer-density workflow development and HPC resource evaluation, building on earlier UMA / FAIR-Chem workflow exploration.
